question: What percentage of total item revenue from delivered orders comes from the top 10 sellers?

/* 1️⃣  Revenue per seller for *delivered* orders */
WITH seller_rev AS (
    SELECT
        oi.seller_id,
        SUM(oi.price * oi.quantity) AS rev
    FROM order_items AS oi
    JOIN orders AS o
          ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.status = 'delivered'                -- only delivered orders
    GROUP BY oi.seller_id
),

/* 2️⃣  Total revenue from all delivered orders */

    SELECT SUM(rev) AS total
    FROM seller_rev
),

/* 3️⃣  Revenue contributed by the top‑10 sellers */

    SELECT rev
    FROM seller_rev
    ORDER BY rev DESC
    LIMIT 10
)

/* 4️⃣  Final percentage */

    ROUND(100.0 * (SELECT SUM(rev) FROM top10_rev) /
               (SELECT total   FROM total_rev), 2) AS pct_top10_seller_rev
;

/* --------------------------------------------------------------

   This query returns four key numbers that together tell you
   how satisfied your customers are:

question: Which product category (English name) sold the most items in delivered orders that got a 5-star review?

/*  Which product category (English name) sold the most items
    in delivered orders that received a 5‑star review?          */
SELECT
    c.name_en                     AS category_name,
    SUM(oi.quantity)              AS total_items_sold
FROM orders AS o
JOIN reviews AS r
      ON r.order_id = o.order_id
     AND r.rating   = 5                     -- only 5‑star reviews
JOIN order_items AS oi
      ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN products AS p
      ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN categories AS c
      ON c.category_id = p.category_id
WHERE o.status = 'delivered'                -- only delivered orders
GROUP BY c.category_id, c.name_en
ORDER BY total_items_sold DESC
LIMIT 1;                                    -- the top‑selling category

question: For each year, show the number of delivered orders, the total item revenue and the total amount paid.

/* --------------------------------------------------------------
   Assumed schema (feel free to rename the columns/tables to match yours)

   orders
   -------
   order_id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY
   order_date        TEXT      -- ISO‑8601 date‑time string (e.g. '2023-07-15')
   delivery_date     TEXT      -- NULL until the order is delivered
   status            TEXT      -- e.g. 'pending', 'shipped', 'delivered', …
   total_paid        NUMERIC   -- amount the customer paid (incl. taxes, fees)

   order_items
   -----------
   order_item_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY
   order_id          INTEGER   -- FK → orders.order_id
   product_id        INTEGER
   unit_price        NUMERIC   -- price per unit at the time of sale
   quantity          INTEGER   -- number of units sold
   -------------------------------------------------------------- */

SELECT
    strftime('%Y', o.delivery_date)                AS year,
    COUNT(*)                                       AS delivered_orders,
    SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity)               AS total_item_revenue,
    SUM(o.total_paid)                              AS total_amount_paid
FROM
    orders      AS o
    JOIN order_items AS oi
          ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE
    o.status = 'delivered'                -- only delivered orders
    AND o.delivery_date IS NOT NULL        -- safety check
GROUP BY
    strftime('%Y', o.delivery_date)
ORDER BY
    year;

p AS (SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid FROM order_payments GROUP BY order_id)

       ROUND(SUM(i.rev), 2) AS revenue, ROUND(SUM(p.paid), 2) AS paid

/* --------------------------------------------------------------
   Are our customers happy?
   --------------------------------------------------------------
   This query returns four key numbers that together tell you
   how satisfied your customers are:

   1️⃣ total_feedback      – how many feedback entries we have
   2️⃣ happy_customers    – count of feedback with a “happy” rating
   3️⃣ avg_rating          – average rating (scale 1‑5, higher = happier)
   4️⃣ happy_percentage    – % of feedback that is “happy”

   Adjust the rating threshold (here 4) if you consider a different
   score to be “happy”.
   -------------------------------------------------------------- */

SELECT
    COUNT(*)                                            AS total_feedback,
    SUM(CASE WHEN rating >= 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)       AS happy_customers,
    ROUND(AVG(rating), 2)                               AS avg_rating,
    ROUND(100.0 *
          SUM(CASE WHEN rating >= 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) /
          COUNT(*), 2)                                 AS happy_percentage
FROM feedback;

/* 1️⃣  Revenue per seller for *delivered* orders */
WITH seller_rev AS (
    SELECT
        oi.seller_id,
        SUM(oi.price * oi.quantity) AS rev
    FROM order_items AS oi
    JOIN orders AS o
          ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.status = 'delivered'                -- only delivered orders
    GROUP BY oi.seller_id
),

/* 2️⃣  Total revenue from all delivered orders */
total_rev AS (
    SELECT SUM(rev) AS total
    FROM seller_rev
),

/* 3️⃣  Revenue of the top‑10 sellers (by revenue) */
top10_rev AS (
    SELECT rev
    FROM seller_rev
    ORDER BY rev DESC
    LIMIT 10
)

    ROUND(
        100.0 * (SELECT SUM(rev) FROM top10_rev)   -- revenue of top‑10
        / (SELECT total FROM total_rev),           -- total delivered revenue
        2)                                          -- round to 2 decimal places
    AS pct_revenue_top_10_sellers;

question: What were our sales last month?

WITH max_date AS (
    SELECT MAX(order_purchase_timestamp) AS max_ts
    FROM orders
),
target_month AS (
    SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', date(max_ts, '-1 month')) AS ym
    FROM max_date
),
order_rev AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(price) AS revenue
    FROM order_items
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT SUM(orv.revenue) AS sales
FROM orders o
JOIN order_rev orv ON o.order_id = orv.order_id
JOIN target_month tm ON strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_purchase_timestamp) = tm.ym
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered';
